### T-148 — Family and species edit tests still rename the seeded row

> _2026-09-24 · demo/blong-marine · done_

The family and species edit tests still open the first row of the unfiltered browse table and rename
it, because on those two pages the browse search does not isolate the record the spec created: the
marine family and species lists are served by the mocked models (meta/db/db.ts), and the capture
comes out byte-identical with and without a search pin, while habitat (also mocked) does honour it.
The damage is visible rather than fatal: the family rename is what the coral pages show in their
left tree, so every coral capture taken in the same run as family.play.ts carries a test family
name, and a species capture carries the renamed species. It stays cosmetic because the documented
regeneration command runs the docs spec alone (a fresh process seeds the mocks from marineYaml), so
the fix is worth doing only with the mock behaviour understood - what to establish first is whether
a mocked model list is supposed to filter at all, and if not, whether the family and species specs
should carry their own record through a different route (as the coral spec now does for the
navigator).

Family and species specs pin their own record (search plus navigatorNode for species); their
open/edit baselines were re-captured. See D-621.

### T-599 — The family tree error is not the reserved order column

> _2026-11-02 · demo/blong-marine · done_

The reserved word is not the cause, and the one call the report named cannot produce the error.
Checked against the deployment itself rather than the tree: the pods run the v1.16.0 code (their
`knex.ts` differs from the tag only in an import path), `marine.family.find` is a registered route
on the marine pod, and `demo/blong-marine/meta/db/db.ts` in that image declares
`mock: {marineFamilyModel: true, marineSpeciesModel: true, marineHabitatModel: true}` — so the
family list is answered from the fixture and never reaches SQL. `knex.generic` is the bare `switch`
fallthrough in `exec`, reachable only by a verb outside
`get/find/add/edit/remove/merge/insert/update/delete`, and `find` is one of them.

The call that did fall through stays unattributed, and cannot be replayed: the session left no
request log (the throw is a declared error, so the logging boundary records nothing), and an MLE
login through a port-forward to the pod does not complete, so the deployment cannot be driven from
here.

What the next occurrence costs is now the point of the change: the refusal names the method and the
verb it could not serve, in the log and in the message the dialog shows
(`Knex Error: no operation for {operation} in {method}`, `knexError.test.ts`). Found on the way that
`knex.missingKey` passed its value outside `params`, the map the factory interpolates, so a missing
key rendered `Missing key value for ?key?`; both call sites and the message are fixed and tested.

Nothing needs renaming: `order` is a reserved word only in a clause that names it unquoted, and knex
backticks every identifier it is handed — a live sort reaches MySQL as an ordering by the backticked
column (`D-742`).

Closed as: the reserved word is not the cause (the family read is mocked in the deployed image, and
knex backticks what it names), the named call cannot reach the fallthrough, and the event cannot be
replayed. The remaining value is the guard: knex.generic now names the method and verb in its
message (knexError.test.ts), and knex.missingKey's param shape is fixed.
